Make this Valentine's run deliver installs. We're Orbiloom, based in Auckland, and our iPhone journaling app helps people notice and record small things they appreciate about someone they love. Installs are what we count; get as many as possible.

Run from Wednesday, February 10, 2027 through Sunday, February 14, 2027, inclusive: five days in the account's time zone, Auckland time. Valentine's Day is Sunday, February 14, so keep the collection's unlock deadline accurate throughout the run.

Send people to https://orbiloom.app/love. Here's the copy from our landing page:
"Made in Auckland, Orbiloom is a free iPhone journaling app with one daily prompt for noticing the small things you appreciate about someone you love. Install by February 14, 2027 to unlock our 14-day Things I Notice prompt collection free, a little Valentine's gift for yourself or someone you love. Available worldwide except Iran, North Korea, Cuba and Syria. Only for iPhone (iOS)."

Everything is localized: the app and the landing page come in every major language, and we have a version of each post in every market's language, so people everywhere see us in their own language.

Our site does not have X's pixel, so X can't see the installs. Our posts and landing page do the work: people tap through to the page and install the iPhone app from the App Store from there. There's no app-install campaign or app ID to set up. The product only exists for iPhone.

You have authority to launch and manage the campaign yourself without asking me for approval. Watch it throughout the full flight and make adjustments as needed. I expect active management. At the end, send me a short recap with spend, impressions and link clicks. Keep those figures clearly separate from installs.

Total budget: 350.00 USD for everything you launch: every campaign and ad group draws on this one budget. We've approved these 4 posts, all on our account, and only these, so please don't write new ones. Promote whichever you think will work, in as many campaigns and ad groups as you like, and change, pause or stop them as you learn what works:
